units.title: Cyrillic: familiar shapes and false friends
goals: Read twelve Cyrillic letters in print, capital and small: 'а', 'к', 'м', 'о', 'т', 'в', 'е', 'н', 'р', 'с', 'у', 'х'
Tell the letters that look and sound like English letters from the false friends that look alike and sound different
Read the stress mark this course writes on every word of two or more syllables, and say an unstressed 'о' as 'а'
Read and say first words and phrases such as 'ма́ма', 'Москва́' and 'Кто там?'
grammar: The Cyrillic alphabet: 33 letters, of which this unit teaches twelve
Letters with the same shape and nearly the same sound: 'а', 'к', 'м', 'о', 'т'
False friends: 'в' [v], 'е' [je], 'н' [n], 'р' [r], 'с' [s], 'у' [u], 'х' [x]
The stress mark, and the first rule of vowel reduction: unstressed 'о' is said like 'а'
Sentences with no verb for 'is', met as a pattern ('Ма́ма тут'), and 'вот' for pointing out
vocabulary_themes: words chosen only from the twelve letters of the unit

units.title: New letters for familiar sounds, and voicing
goals: Read ten more letters: 'б', 'г', 'д', 'з', 'и', 'й', 'л', 'п', 'ф', 'э'
Pair the voiced and voiceless consonants and say a voiced consonant at the end of a word as its voiceless partner
Apply voicing assimilation in consonant clusters, as in 'вокза́л'
Name things and ask where they are with 'э́то' and 'где'
grammar: New shapes for familiar sounds: 'б', 'г', 'д', 'з', 'л', 'п', 'ф', and the vowels 'и' and 'э', and 'й'
Voiced and voiceless pairs: 'б' and 'п', 'в' and 'ф', 'г' and 'к', 'д' and 'т', 'з' and 'с'
Final devoicing ('хлеб', 'друг', 'го́род') and assimilation in clusters ('вокза́л')
Sentences with 'э́то' ('Э́то дом') and questions with 'где'
Joining with 'и' and contrasting with 'а'

units.title: Hard and soft: paired vowel letters and the two signs
goals: Read the remaining vowel letters 'я', 'ё', 'ю', 'ы' and the signs 'ь' and 'ъ'
Explain how the vowel letter after a consonant shows whether the consonant is hard or soft
Say soft consonants, the vowel 'ы' and the separate [j] that 'ь' and 'ъ' mark before a vowel
Explain why 'ё' never needs a stress mark
grammar: Hard and soft consonants, and the two series of vowel letters: 'а', 'э', 'ы', 'о', 'у' and 'я', 'е', 'и', 'ё', 'ю'
'я', 'е', 'ё', 'ю' as [ja], [je], [jo], [ju] at the start of a word and after a vowel
The soft sign 'ь' after a consonant ('соль', 'день'), and 'ь' and 'ъ' before a vowel ('семья́', 'подъе́зд')
The vowel 'ы' and minimal pairs such as 'был' and 'бил'
'ё', always stressed
vocabulary_themes: words chosen to show hard and soft consonants

units.title: Hushing sounds, the spelling rules and the whole alphabet
goals: Read 'ж', 'ш', 'щ', 'ч' and 'ц', and know which consonants are always hard and which always soft
Apply the two spelling rules that govern 'и' and 'ы', 'а' and 'я', 'у' and 'ю' after certain consonants
Say the 33 letters in order with their names and spell a name aloud
Recognize the italic and handwritten letter forms that differ from print
grammar: The hushing consonants 'ж', 'ш', 'щ', 'ч' and the consonant 'ц'
Always hard 'ж', 'ш', 'ц'; always soft 'ч', 'щ', 'й'
Spelling rule 1: 'и', never 'ы', after 'г', 'к', 'х', 'ж', 'ш', 'ч', 'щ'; spelling rule 2: 'а' and 'у', never 'я' and 'ю', after 'ж', 'ш', 'ч', 'щ', 'ц'
The alphabet in order and the letter names
Italic and handwritten forms
vocabulary_themes: school and things in a bag
spelling aloud with the letter names

units.title: Stress and vowel reduction
goals: Explain that Russian stress can fall on any syllable, can move between forms of a word, and can distinguish words
Apply the reduction rules for unstressed 'о', 'а', 'е' and 'я'
Read the common words not pronounced as spelled, such as 'что', 'сего́дня' and 'здра́вствуйте'
Read any new word aloud with a complete procedure
grammar: Free and mobile stress ('сестра́' and 'сёстры'); words told apart by stress ('за́мок' and 'замо́к')
Reduction of 'о' and 'а' ([ɐ] and [ə]) and of 'е', 'я' and 'а' after soft consonants ([ɪ])
Unstressed one-syllable words read with the next word
'г' as [v] in '-ого', '-его', 'его́' and 'сего́дня'; 'ч' as [ʂ] in 'что' and 'коне́чно'; silent consonants; 'сч' as [ɕː]; '-тся' and '-ться' as [tsə]
vocabulary_themes: words chosen to show stress and reduction
common words read differently from their spelling

units.title: How Russian works: words, gender and verbs
goals: Name the parts of speech and the terms of grammar used in the course, in English and in Russian
Explain how a Russian sentence differs from an English one: no articles, no verb for 'is' in the present, flexible word order and questions by intonation
Tell the gender of a noun from its ending and replace a noun with 'он', 'она́' or 'оно́'
Explain how a verb changes for person and number, using 'знать', and what tense and aspect mean
Choose between 'ты' and 'вы'
grammar: Parts of speech and the vocabulary of grammar ('существи́тельное', 'прилага́тельное', 'глаго́л', 'оконча́ние', 'род', 'число́')
No articles; no verb for 'is' in the present; the written dash between two nouns
Gender from the ending, masculine nouns in '-а' and '-я', nouns in '-ь', and agreement
The personal pronouns, and 'ты' and 'вы'
Verbs: the infinitive, conjugation by person and number ('зна́ю', 'зна́ешь'), three tenses and two aspects
Word order, questions by intonation, and 'не' before the word it negates
vocabulary_themes: the particle 'не', the conjunctions 'но' and 'и́ли', and the adverb 'то́же'

units.title: How Russian works: the cases
goals: Explain what a case is and why Russian nouns change their endings
Name the six cases and the main job of each
Ask the question word that belongs to each case
Explain why Russian word order can change without changing who does what
grammar: Case as a form that shows a word's job; English traces in 'I' and 'me', 'who' and 'whom'
The six cases: nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, instrumental, prepositional, with their Russian names
Question words by case: 'кто', 'кого́', 'кому́', 'кем', 'о ком'; 'что', 'чего́', 'чему́', 'чем', 'о чём'
Prepositions that require a case; animate and inanimate nouns
One model noun in all six cases, for recognition ('кни́га', 'кни́ги', 'кни́ге', 'кни́гу', 'кни́гой', 'о кни́ге')
vocabulary_themes: animals and letters, for examples of who does what to whom

units.title: Greetings and introductions
goals: Greet people and say goodbye in informal and formal situations
Introduce yourself and ask someone's name with 'Как тебя́ зову́т?' and 'Как вас зову́т?'
Say your nationality and what you do, in sentences with no verb
Use the basic politeness expressions and say what each one literally means
grammar: Informal and formal greetings and farewells: 'приве́т', 'пока́', 'здра́вствуйте', 'до свида́ния'
'Меня́ зову́т...' as a fixed pattern, with 'меня́', 'тебя́' and 'вас'
Identity sentences with pronoun subjects: 'Я студе́нт', 'Вы америка́нец?'
Nationality words: 'америка́нец', 'америка́нка', 'ру́сский', 'ру́сская'
'Как дела́?', 'о́чень прия́тно', 'спаси́бо', 'пожа́луйста', 'извини́те'

units.title: Family: gender, plural and possessives
goals: Talk about the members of your family
Form the nominative plural of nouns, including the common irregular plurals
Say whose something is with 'мой', 'твой', 'наш', 'ваш', 'его́', 'её', 'их' and ask with 'чей'
grammar: Gender in practice, with masculine nouns in '-а' such as 'де́душка' and 'мужчи́на'
The nominative plural: '-ы', '-и', '-а', '-я', the stressed '-а́' ('города́') and irregular plurals ('бра́тья', 'де́ти', 'друзья́')
Possessives that agree ('мой', 'моя́', 'моё', 'мои́') and those that never change ('его́', 'её', 'их')
'Чей', 'чья', 'чьё', 'чьи'

units.title: Describing people and things: adjectives
goals: Describe people and things with adjectives that agree with the noun
Apply the spelling rules to adjective endings
Ask what something is like with 'како́й' and point things out with 'э́тот' and 'тот'
Tell 'Э́то кни́га' from 'Э́та кни́га'
grammar: Nominative adjective endings: '-ый', '-ая', '-ое', '-ые'; stressed '-о́й'; soft '-ий', '-яя', '-ее', '-ие'
Spelling rules in endings ('ру́сский', 'хоро́шая', 'хоро́шее', 'большо́е')
Adjectives before the noun and as the predicate
'како́й', 'тако́й', 'э́тот', 'тот', and 'о́чень'

units.title: Work and study: the present tense
goals: Conjugate verbs of both conjugations in the present tense
Say what you do, where you live and which languages you speak
Use the verbs whose stem consonant or stress changes in the present
Tell 'по-ру́сски' from 'ру́сский язы́к'
grammar: Conjugation I ('чита́ю', 'чита́ешь') and conjugation II ('говорю́', 'говори́шь'); stressed 'ё' ('живёшь')
Telling the conjugations apart from the infinitive
Consonant changes and moving stress ('люблю́', 'лю́бишь'; 'пишу́', 'пи́шешь')
'Говори́ть по-ру́сски' and 'изуча́ть ру́сский язы́к'; 'люби́ть' with an infinitive

units.title: Places in the city: the prepositional case
goals: Say where someone or something is with 'в' and 'на' and the prepositional case
Choose between 'в' and 'на' for places
Talk about someone or something with 'о' and the prepositional case
Use the prepositional forms of adjectives, possessives and personal pronouns
grammar: Prepositional singular endings '-е' and '-и', and the stressed '-у́' of 'в саду́', 'в лесу́', 'на мосту́'
'в' for inside, cities and countries; 'на' for surfaces, open places, events and a fixed list ('на рабо́те', 'на по́чте')
Adjectives and possessives: '-ом', '-ем', '-ой', '-ей'
'о' and 'об' with the prepositional; 'обо мне', 'о тебе́', 'о нём', 'о ней'
'стоя́ть' and 'лежа́ть' for where things are

units.title: Food and drink: the accusative case
goals: Say what you want, eat and drink, with the object in the accusative case
Tell animate from inanimate masculine nouns in the accusative
Order food and drink politely in a café
Use the irregular verbs 'хоте́ть', 'есть' and 'пить'
grammar: Accusative singular endings: '-у', '-ю'; inanimate masculine and neuter unchanged; animate masculine '-а', '-я'
Adjectives: '-ую', '-юю'; '-ого', '-его' for animate masculine nouns
Accusative personal pronouns ('меня́', 'тебя́', 'его́', 'её', 'нас', 'вас', 'их')
'хоте́ть', 'есть' and 'пить' in the present; 'на за́втрак'

units.title: Home: having and not having (the genitive case)
goals: Describe your home and say what it has and does not have
Say what you have with 'у меня́ есть' and what you lack with 'нет'
Say whose something is and where someone is from with the genitive case
Use the genitive forms of nouns, adjectives and pronouns, including 'него́', 'неё' and 'них' after prepositions
grammar: Genitive singular endings: '-а', '-я', '-ы', '-и'; adjectives '-ого', '-его', '-ой', '-ей'
Possession: the owner after the noun ('кни́га бра́та')
'У' with the genitive and 'есть' for having; 'нет' with the genitive for absence
'из', 'без' and 'для' with the genitive

units.title: Numbers, time and prices
goals: Count from zero to one thousand
Use the right form of a noun after a number
Tell the time and say on which day something happens
Ask and say what something costs
grammar: Cardinal numbers 0 to 1000; 'оди́н', 'одна́', 'одно́' and 'два', 'две'
A number with a noun: the nominative singular after 1, the genitive singular after 2, 3 and 4, the genitive plural after 5 and more
Telling the time: 'Кото́рый час?', 'два часа́', 'пять часо́в', 'в три часа́'
Days of the week with 'в' and the accusative
'Ско́лько сто́ит?' and rubles
vocabulary_themes: time and the days of the week

units.title: Daily routine: verbs with -ся
goals: Describe a typical day from morning to night
Conjugate verbs with '-ся' and tell those with a reflexive meaning from those without one
Say how often you do something
Tell 'учи́ться' from 'изуча́ть' and 'учи́ть'
grammar: The suffix '-ся' and '-сь'; reflexive and non-reflexive meanings
Verbs in '-ава́ть': 'встаю́', 'встаёшь'
Times of day as adverbs: 'у́тром', 'днём', 'ве́чером', 'но́чью'
Frequency words, and 'никогда́' with 'не'
Sequence words 'снача́ла' and 'пото́м'

units.title: Likes, needs and age: the dative case
goals: Say what you and other people like with 'нра́виться'
Say what someone must, may, needs or cannot do with 'на́до', 'ну́жно', 'мо́жно' and 'нельзя́'
Say how you feel with 'мне хо́лодно' and similar sentences, and say your age
Use the dative for the person who receives or experiences something
grammar: Dative singular endings: '-у', '-ю', '-е', '-и'; adjectives '-ому', '-ему', '-ой', '-ей'; pronouns 'мне', 'тебе́', 'ему́', 'ей', 'нам', 'вам', 'им'
'Мне нра́вится': the thing liked is the subject
Predicatives with the dative and an infinitive; impersonal states ('Мне ску́чно')
Age with 'год', 'го́да', 'лет'
'мочь', 'уме́ть' and 'мо́жно'; verbs that take the dative ('звони́ть', 'помога́ть')

units.title: Jobs and free time: the instrumental case
goals: Say what someone does for a living with 'рабо́тать' and the instrumental
Talk about hobbies with 'занима́ться', 'интересова́ться' and 'игра́ть'
Say who you do something with, using 'с' and the instrumental
Use the instrumental forms of nouns, adjectives and pronouns
grammar: Instrumental singular endings: '-ом', '-ем', '-ой', '-ей', '-ью'; adjectives '-ым', '-им'; pronouns 'мной', 'тобо́й', 'им', 'ей'
'с' with the instrumental, and 'мы с бра́том'
The instrument ('писа́ть ру́чкой') and the role ('рабо́тать врачо́м')
Verbs that take the instrumental; verbs in '-ова́ть' ('интересу́юсь')
'игра́ть в' for games and 'игра́ть на' for instruments

units.title: Going places: идти́, е́хать and direction
goals: Ask and say where someone is going, where they are and where they come from
Choose between 'идти́' and 'е́хать'
Say how you travel, and give and follow simple directions
grammar: 'где', 'куда́' and 'отку́да' with the prepositional, the accusative and the genitive
'в' and 'на' with the accusative for destination; 'из' and 'с' with the genitive for origin; 'к' and 'от' for a person
'идти́' and 'е́хать' in the present
Transport with 'на' and the prepositional; 'пешко́м'
Directions: 'сле́ва', 'спра́ва', 'пря́мо'

units.title: A1 consolidation
goals: Combine A1 grammar in longer conversations
Introduce yourself in detail and ask a newcomer about themselves
Link sentences with 'потому́ что', 'поэ́тому', 'когда́' and 'что'
Avoid the common beginner errors
grammar: Review: the six cases in the singular, the nominative plural, both conjugations, verbs with '-ся', 'идти́' and 'е́хать'
Common errors: 'э́то' and 'э́тот', 'есть', 'нра́виться', 'где' and 'куда́', the animate accusative
Linking words and 'что' as a conjunction
Plans with the present tense

units.title: Past events and dates: the past tense
goals: Say what you did with the past tense, which agrees in gender and number
Say what you had and did not have in the past
Say the date and when something happened with ordinal numbers and months
grammar: The past tense: '-л', '-ла', '-ло', '-ли'; '-лся', '-лась'
'был', 'была́', 'бы́ло', 'бы́ли', and 'не́ был', 'не была́', 'не́ было'
Irregular pasts: 'шёл', 'шла'; 'ел'; 'мог', 'могла́'
Having in the past, and 'не́ было' with the genitive
Ordinal numbers, dates ('пе́рвое ма́я', 'пе́рвого ма́я') and months ('в январе́')

units.title: Aspect: imperfective and perfective
goals: Explain what aspect is and why every Russian verb has one
Recognize how aspect partners are formed
Choose the aspect in the past for a process, a repetition or a completed result
grammar: Imperfective and perfective: process, repetition and fact against one complete action
Pairs formed by a prefix ('сде́лать'), a change of suffix ('реши́ть', 'купи́ть') or a different verb ('сказа́ть', 'взять')
No present tense for perfective verbs; the few verbs of both aspects
Aspect in the past: 'чита́л' and 'прочита́л'; 'до́лго' and 'за час'

units.title: Plans and weather: the future tense
goals: Talk about plans with the imperfective and perfective future
Use the future after 'когда́' and 'е́сли' where English uses the present
Describe the weather and the seasons with impersonal sentences
grammar: 'бу́ду' with an imperfective infinitive; the perfective future
The future of 'быть' ('бу́дет хо́лодно')
'когда́' and 'е́сли' with the future
Impersonal sentences in three tenses; 'идёт дождь'
Seasons as adverbs: 'зимо́й', 'весно́й', 'ле́том', 'о́сенью'
'че́рез' with the accusative for a time from now

units.title: Requests and instructions: the imperative
goals: Form the imperative for 'ты' and 'вы'
Choose the aspect of an imperative for a request, an invitation or a prohibition
Suggest doing something together with 'дава́й' and 'дава́йте'
Follow and give instructions in a class and in a recipe
grammar: Formation from the present or future stem: '-й', '-и', '-ь', and '-те'
'-ся' and '-сь' in the imperative; irregular 'дай', 'ешь', 'пей', 'будь'
Perfective requests, imperfective invitations, and negative instructions in the imperfective
'Дава́й' and 'дава́йте'
The fixed imperatives of A1 explained ('извини́те', 'скажи́те', 'да́йте')
Putting things somewhere: 'класть' and 'положи́ть', 'ста́вить' and 'поста́вить'

units.title: Shopping and quantities: the genitive plural
goals: Form the genitive plural of nouns
Talk about quantities with 'мно́го', 'ма́ло', 'ско́лько' and 'не́сколько'
Buy food by weight, bottle and packet
grammar: Genitive plural endings: '-ов', '-ев', '-ей', and no ending with an inserted vowel ('ру́чек', 'око́н')
Irregular genitive plurals ('люде́й', 'дете́й', 'лет')
Quantity words with the genitive plural or the genitive singular
Containers and measures ('буты́лка молока́', 'кило́ я́блок')

units.title: Friends and guests: the plural in every case
goals: Use nouns, adjectives and possessives in the plural in every case
Form the accusative plural of animate and inanimate nouns
Talk about groups of people: guests, friends and colleagues
grammar: Dative '-ам', instrumental '-ами', prepositional '-ах' for every gender
The accusative plural: the nominative for inanimate nouns, the genitive for animate ones
Plural adjectives in every case: '-ых', '-ым', '-ыми'
'весь' in every form; common-gender nouns such as 'колле́га'
'по' with the dative, and 'по' with the plural for repeated times ('по суббо́там')

units.title: Relationships: свой, себя́ and verbs that choose a case
goals: Choose between 'свой' and 'его́', 'её', 'их'
Use 'себя́', 'друг дру́га' and 'сам'
Use the verbs whose case differs from the English construction
Talk about meeting people, marriage and arguments
grammar: 'свой', referring to the subject
'себя́' and 'друг дру́га', with a preposition between the two words
Emphatic 'сам'
Verbs with a particular case: 'боя́ться' with the genitive, 'ве́рить' with the dative, 'встреча́ться с', 'поздравля́ть с', 'благодари́ть за'
'жени́ться на', 'вы́йти за́муж за', 'жена́т', 'за́мужем'

units.title: Verbs of motion: one direction and many
goals: Choose between a unidirectional verb such as 'идти́' and a multidirectional verb such as 'ходи́ть'
Say where you went and came back with the multidirectional past
Talk about carrying, leading and transporting
grammar: Unidirectional and multidirectional verbs: 'идти́' and 'ходи́ть', 'е́хать' and 'е́здить', 'лете́ть' and 'лета́ть', 'бежа́ть' and 'бе́гать', 'плыть' and 'пла́вать'
Uses: one direction now, or repetition, round trips, ability and movement with no single direction
The past of a round trip ('ходи́л в кино́') and of a journey as background ('шёл')
'нести́' and 'носи́ть', 'вести́' and 'води́ть', 'везти́' and 'вози́ть'

units.title: Prefixed verbs of motion
goals: Form prefixed verbs of motion and their aspect pairs
Use the main prefixes to say arriving, leaving, entering, going out, crossing and dropping in
Give and follow detailed directions in a city
grammar: A prefix on a unidirectional verb makes a perfective; on a multidirectional verb, its imperfective partner ('прийти́' and 'приходи́ть')
The prefixes 'при-', 'у-', 'в-', 'вы-', 'пере-', 'до-', 'за-', 'про-', 'под-', 'от-'
Matching prepositions: 'в' and 'из', 'на' and 'с', 'к' and 'от', 'до', 'ми́мо'
'пойти́' and 'пое́хать' for setting off; 'принести́'

units.title: Health, the body and short adjectives
goals: Name parts of the body and describe symptoms
Say what hurts with 'боли́т' and that you are ill with 'бо́лен' or 'больна́'
Use short adjectives such as 'рад', 'до́лжен' and 'ну́жен'
Understand and give simple medical advice
grammar: Two verbs written 'боле́ть': 'боле́ю' (to be ill) and 'боли́т' (to hurt)
Short adjectives: their endings and their use as the predicate
'до́лжен' with an infinitive; 'ну́жен' agreeing with the thing needed
'чу́вствовать себя́'; advice with the imperative and 'на́до'

units.title: Comparing: comparatives and superlatives
goals: Compare two people or things
Say that something is the best, the biggest or the most interesting
Say how much bigger or older something is
grammar: The simple comparative in '-ее' and the irregular comparatives ('лу́чше', 'бо́льше', 'доро́же')
'чем' with the same case as the thing compared, or the genitive without 'чем'
'бо́лее' and 'ме́нее' with an adjective; the superlative with 'са́мый'
'гора́здо', 'намно́го', and 'на' with the accusative for a difference; 'чем..., тем...'

units.title: A2 consolidation
goals: Tell a story in the past with the right aspects
Write a short informal or formal message
Handle everyday problems: canceling, postponing, exchanging and complaining
Avoid the common A2 errors
grammar: Review: the past, the future and aspect; the imperative; plural cases; verbs of motion
Connectors: 'по́сле э́того', 'пока́', 'е́сли', 'хотя́'
Common errors: aspect after 'когда́' and 'е́сли', 'ходи́л' and 'пошёл', 'свой' and 'его́'
Message formulas: 'Приве́т!', 'Здра́вствуйте', 'С уваже́нием'

units.title: Aspect in depth
goals: Use the imperfective past for the bare fact of an action and for a result that has been undone
Choose the aspect in a negative sentence in the past
Choose the aspect of an infinitive after verbs of beginning and ending and after 'нельзя́' and 'не на́до'
grammar: The imperfective of general fact ('Вы чита́ли...?') and of an undone result ('Кто открыва́л окно́?')
'не звони́л' and 'не позвони́л'
The imperfective infinitive after 'нача́ть', 'ко́нчить', 'продолжа́ть', 'уста́ть', 'надое́сть'
'нельзя́' with the imperfective and with the perfective; 'не на́до' and 'не сто́ит'; 'успе́ть'

units.title: People and places described: кото́рый
goals: Join sentences with 'кото́рый' in every case
Use 'тот, кто' and 'то, что'
Describe people, places and works of art in detail
grammar: 'кото́рый': gender and number from its noun, case from its own clause
Prepositions before 'кото́рый', and 'кото́рого' for 'whose'
'тот, кто', 'те, кто', 'то, что'
'где', 'куда́' and 'отку́да' as relatives; 'тако́й, како́й'

units.title: If and would: the conditional
goals: Talk about unreal situations with 'е́сли бы'
Make polite requests and wishes with 'бы'
Give advice with 'на твоём ме́сте я бы'
grammar: The conditional: the past form with the particle 'бы', with no tenses
The position of 'бы'
Real conditions with the indicative and unreal conditions with 'бы'
'Я бы хоте́л', 'Вы не могли́ бы...?', 'хорошо́ бы'

units.title: Wishes and purposes: что́бы
goals: Say why you do something with 'что́бы'
Say what you want or ask someone else to do with 'что́бы' and the past form
Express wishes and propose toasts
grammar: 'что́бы' with an infinitive for the same subject and with the past form for a different subject
'хоте́ть', 'проси́ть', 'сказа́ть', 'ва́жно' with 'что́бы'
'пусть' with the third person; 'мне хо́чется'
'жела́ть' with the dative and the genitive; toasts with 'за'
'разреша́ть' and 'запреща́ть' with the dative

units.title: Reported speech
goals: Report statements, questions and requests
Ask an indirect yes-or-no question with 'ли'
Explain why Russian keeps the tense of the original words
grammar: Statements with 'что' and the tense of the original
Indirect yes-or-no questions with 'ли'; questions with a question word
Requests with 'что́бы' and the past form
Reporting verbs and their aspect pairs

units.title: Nobody and somebody: negative and indefinite pronouns
goals: Use negative words such as 'никто́' and 'ничего́' with 'не'
Say that there is nobody to talk to or nothing to do with 'не́кого' and 'не́чего'
Choose between '-то' and '-нибудь'
grammar: Negative words with 'ни-' and double negation; a preposition between 'ни' and the pronoun ('ни с кем')
'не́кого', 'не́чего', 'не́где', 'не́когда' with an infinitive and the dative
'-то' for a definite unknown and '-нибудь' for any
One stress mark on a hyphenated word ('кто́-то')

units.title: Numbers in every case, years and quantities
goals: Use numbers in every case with the noun in the right form
Say years and full dates
Use collective numbers, fractions and percentages, and give approximate quantities
grammar: The declension of cardinal numbers; 'ты́сяча' and 'миллио́н' as nouns
Collective numbers 'дво́е', 'тро́е'; 'о́ба' and 'о́бе'
Years with an ordinal ('в две ты́сячи пя́том году́') and full dates
Approximation ('лет пять', 'о́коло'), fractions and percentages
Clock times with minutes ('полови́на второ́го', 'без пяти́ три')

units.title: Work, opinions and formal register
goals: Address people formally in speech and in writing
Write a formal letter and a cover letter
Give, defend and soften an opinion, and agree or disagree politely
grammar: 'вы' with the name and patronymic; 'Вы' in letters
Agreement with 'вы': plural verbs and short adjectives
Formal letter formulas: 'Уважа́емый', 'С уваже́нием', 'Бу́дьте добры́'
Opinions: 'по-мо́ему', 'мне ка́жется', 'я счита́ю', 'я согла́сен'

units.title: Active participles
goals: Form present and past active participles
Replace a 'кото́рый' clause with a participle phrase and back
Read news reports that use participles
grammar: The participle as a verb form with adjective endings
Present active: '-щий' from the 'они́' form; past active: '-вший' and '-ший'
Participle phrases before and after the noun, with commas
Words that began as participles ('бу́дущий', 'сле́дующий', 'настоя́щий')
vocabulary_themes: people described by what they do

units.title: The passive: passive participles and verbs with -ся
goals: Form past passive participles and their short forms
Use the three Russian passives: '-ся', the short participle and the third person plural
Talk about inventions, discoveries and history
grammar: Imperfective verbs with '-ся' as a passive
Past passive participles in '-нный', '-енный' and '-тый', and short forms with 'быть'
The agent in the instrumental ('напи́сана Толсты́м')
Present passive participles in '-емый' and '-имый'
The third person plural with no subject ('Здесь говоря́т по-англи́йски')

units.title: Verbal adverbs
goals: Form imperfective and perfective verbal adverbs
Use a verbal adverb for a second action of the same subject
Recognize the subject rule and why breaking it is a well-known error
grammar: The verbal adverb ('дееприча́стие'): an unchanging verb form for a second action
Imperfective '-я', '-а'; perfective '-в', '-вшись', and '-я' for verbs of motion in '-йти'
Simultaneous and earlier actions
The subject rule and Chekhov's joke
Adverbs and prepositions that began as verbal adverbs ('мо́лча', 'несмотря́ на')

units.title: Word formation: roots, prefixes and suffixes
goals: Break a word into its root, prefix and suffixes and guess its meaning
Use verbal prefixes for starting, redoing and finishing
Use and understand diminutives and the figurative uses of verbs of motion
grammar: Roots and word families
Verbal prefixes: 'за-', 'пере-', 'до-', 'раз-'
Figurative verbs of motion ('идёт фильм', 'вести́ себя́')
Noun suffixes '-тель', '-ник', '-ость', '-ние', '-ка'; adjective suffixes
Diminutives and their emotional meaning

units.title: Spoken Russian: particles, word order and intonation
goals: Use particles such as 'же', 'ведь', 'ра́зве' and 'неуже́ли' to show attitude
Move words for emphasis and use the main intonation patterns
Recognize colloquial forms and choose the register for a situation
grammar: Attitude particles: 'же', 'ведь', 'ну', 'вот', 'ра́зве', 'неуже́ли', 'да́же'
Word order for emphasis
Intonation of statements, questions and contrasts
Colloquial forms and discourse words ('зна́чит', 'в о́бщем', 'коро́че')

units.title: Reading Russian literature
goals: Read short excerpts of Russian poetry and prose
Recognize literary word order, older forms and figures of speech
Discuss a text's meaning and form
grammar: Literary word order
Older and poetic forms ('-ою', 'одино́кой')
Figures of speech: comparison, metaphor, personification, the epithet
Participles and verbal adverbs in narrative prose

units.title: Formal writing and the language of documents
goals: Write a formal application and an official letter
Use verbal nouns and formal connectors
Write a structured essay and punctuate it correctly
grammar: Verbal nouns and the nominal style; chains of genitives
Formal connectors: 'одна́ко', 'тем не ме́нее', 'сле́довательно', 'таки́м о́бразом'
Prepositions of written style: 'в связи́ с', 'в тече́ние', 'благодаря́', 'согла́сно'
Application, letter and essay structure
The written superlative: 'наибо́лее' and '-ейший'
Commas, and the dash between two nouns in written Russian

units.title: B2 capstone: argument and nuance
goals: Argue a position with nuance and concede a point
Move between conversational, debating and written registers
Combine all the tenses, aspects, moods and constructions of the course
grammar: Review of the cases, aspect, participles, verbal adverbs, the conditional and 'что́бы'
Concession: 'хотя́', 'несмотря́ на то что', 'что бы ни', 'как бы ни'
Emphasis: 'и́менно', 'как раз', 'всё-таки'
Register switching
